title: Jim McCartney dies | 1976
content:
Paul McCartney’s father Jim died on 18 March 1976.

James ‘Jim’ McCartney had been born on 7 July 1902. He married Mary Patricia Mohan on 15 April 1941, and their sons Paul and Michael were born in 1942 and 1944 respectively. Mary died in October 1956, and in November 1964 Jim married Angela Williams and adopted her daughter Ruth from a previous marriage. They lived together in Rembrandt, a bungalow bought by Paul in Heswall, Cheshire.

Jim’s health had been in decline since the early 1970s. By the beginning of 1976 Paul was calling the house almost daily to check on him, and Angie was paying £300 a year for a doctor to check his health each Tuesday.

Aware that the decline was terminal, Paul and Linda visited Rembrandt on 13 March. Upon their arrival, Cynthia Lennon and former Fourmost member Billy Hatton were also there. Jim mostly slept, but was frequently delirious when awake.

The McCartneys returned to the house the next day, but were unable to stay in the region any longer. On Wednesday 17 March, he called Angie from London, and asked her to promise that Paul would be the first to hear should the worst happen to Jim.

That call came the next day. Jim’s reprted final words were “I’ll be with Mary soon.”

Wings were at a press launch for the Wings At The Speed Of Sound album at London’s Palace Hotel, when MPL’s publicist Tony Brainsby informed Paul that Angie McCartney was calling with urgent news.

Jim McCartney’s death notice appeared in the Liverpool Echo the next day. George Harrison and Ringo Starr sent flowers to Angie, along with donations to Leasowe Hospital.

McCARTNEY—March 18, 1976, peacefully at home, 20 Beverley Drive, Gayton, Wirral. JAMES McCARTNEY, beloved husband of Angela, and dear father of Paul, Michael and Ruth. Private service in his residence, Monday, March 22, followed by cremation at Landican, at 10.30 a.m. No flowers please, but donations may be sent for Arthritis Research, c/o Doctor T.R. Littler, Leasowe Hospital, Wirral.

Despite his deep upset, Paul McCartney kept the news to himself. The former Beatles rarely went to funerals, to avoid taking attention away from the deceased, but he did not mention his loss to the other members of Wings until the end of their European tour in late March.

I was font of Jim McCartney and knew him well but Paul didn’t even tell me he was dead. I found out about it during an interview for French television. We were all sitting in a row and the interviewer asked Paul in broken English if his parents were still alive.

When Paul answered no, I was stunned. I knew his mother had died when he was 14 but he had never mentioned a word to me about his father. I couldn’t believe that Paul would have to be forced into talking of his father’s death by a direct question from an interviewer before he would own up to it.

Paul loved his dad – there is no doubt about that. But death scares him and he didn’t go to the funeral because he couldn’t handle it. It wasn’t lack of love that kept him away – he didn’t want to cry in public.

Denny Laine
The Sun, 2 February 1984

Jim McCartney’s funeral took place on 22 March 1976. He was cremated at Landican Cemetery.

It was no coincidence that Paul was on the continent at the time of the funeral… Paul would never face that sort of thing. As Dad would say, ‘It’s just the way you’re made, son.’
Mike McCartney
